moduleTitle: Section 8 - API Theory & Create API TestCases
learningObjectives: Convert an API TestCase into a functioning Template.
Link values from the TestSheet to the API Template.
Instantiate the API Template and run the TemplateInstances.
Build a concrete API TestCase (Verify Product by SKU) using Common Parameters and the correct Insert/Verify ActionModes.

elements.text: Scenario: test that countries and country IDs are combined correctly by the system. You're given a subset directly from the developer and a TestSheet from the Test Design Specialist, and need to build the TestCases for this new DemoWebShop functionality.

elements.description: Tosca can scan an application's API to collect relevant Request/Response pairs and export them as a raw TestCase. In this course, developers already performed the scan for you. The exported raw TestCase needs adjusting: TestSteps must be renamed and polished, following a clear, consistent structure and naming convention so anyone can follow the flow. The final structure should resemble a UI TestCase — easier to understand and to automate.

elements.text: Want to go deeper into API Scanning itself? See the dedicated "Automation Specialist for API" course.

studyGuide.sectionTitle: The One Key Difference from UI TestCases

elements.text: Like ordering at a restaurant — you can't receive food without placing an order first, and an order is pointless without a response (your food) coming back.

In API TestCases, every Message that performs a function must be expressed as a Request + Response TestStep PAIR. A Request without a Response (or vice versa) is incomplete and must be fixed before proceeding.

studyGuide.sectionTitle: Building the API Template (Same Flow as UI)

elements.title: From raw export to working Template
items: Clean up the exported raw TestCase: rename/polish TestSteps into a clear, consistent structure.
Convert the TestCase to a Template — identical process to UI Templates.
Link the Template to the provided TestSheet.
Link the individual TestSheet Attributes to the Template's TestStepValues.
Check Template for errors, then Instantiate — creating the TemplateInstances.
Run the TestCases to test the new DemoWebShop functionality.

elements.text: Besides the Request/Response pairing requirement, the entire Template workflow (linking, Conditions, Check Template, Instantiate) is IDENTICAL to UI test automation — nothing new to learn mechanically, just a different kind of TestStep.

Scenario: some DemoWebShop products recently had their SKU changed. Since the SKU isn't visible on the UI, you need an API TestCase — "Verify Product by SKU" — to check that BlueJeans still has the expected SKU/ID, using the API Scan subset the developers provided.

elements.title: Create and fill the TestCase
items: Under the TestCase root, create a folder "API", then inside it a folder "8a API TestCase".
Create a TestCase named "Verify Product by SKU" in that folder.
Add the Module "GetProductBySku" and "GetProductBySku Response" to the TestCase.
Fill in the request values: sku = BlueJeans (ActionMode Insert), usernameOrEmail = {CP[Email]} (Insert), userPassword = {CP[Password]} (Insert).
Fill in the response values to verify: Id = 36 (ActionMode Verify), Name = Blue Jeans (Verify).
Set the TestCase WorkState to Completed, then run it in the Scratchbook.

elements.description: {CP[Email]} and {CP[Password]} reference reusable, project-wide Configuration Parameters (e.g. login credentials) — not a TestSheet. They can be dropped into any TestStepValue directly, independent of Attribute/Instance linking, which is why they show up here before any TestSheet is even linked in 8a.

elements.text: Use the correct ActionMode for each direction: request values (sku, usernameOrEmail, userPassword) use Insert; Response values you're checking (Id, Name) use Verify. Mixing these up is the most common mistake in this exercise.

studyGuide.sectionTitle: Exercise 8b: Convert to Template, Link Values, Instantiate

elements.title: Templatize it, exactly like a UI TestCase
items: Duplicate the "8a API TestCase" folder and rename it "8b Convert to Template, Link Values and Instantiate".
Convert the "Verify Product by SKU" TestCase to a Template.
Link the "Verify Product by SKU" TestSheet (TestCaseDesign → "8 API") to the Template.
Link the TestSheet Attributes to the TestStepValues: sku → {XL[sku]}, usernameOrEmail → {XL[Email]}, userPassword → {XL[Password]}, Id → {XL[Id]}, Name → {XL[Name]}.
Delete any extra/leftover Value still sitting next to a newly-linked XL path.
Instantiate the Template, then run the TemplateInstances in the Scratchbook.

elements.text: Before dragging and dropping Values from the TestSheet onto the Template, delete the existing Values in the TestStepValues first — same rule as everywhere else in this course: Tosca appends the new XL reference instead of replacing an existing value.

examPitfalls.title: Leaving a Request without its matching Response (or vice versa)
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Candidates copy over API TestSteps from the raw export without verifying every Message is a complete Request+Response pair.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Each API Message must be expressed as a Request AND Response TestStep pair — one without the other is incomplete.

examPitfalls.title: Assuming API Templates need a totally different workflow
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Learners think API TestCase Templates require new/different Tosca mechanics compared to UI Templates.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Once TestSteps are cleaned up, the Template workflow (link TestSheet, link Values, add Conditions, Check Template, Instantiate) is exactly the same as for UI TestCases.

examPitfalls.title: Using the wrong ActionMode on Response values
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Candidates set Response TestStepValues (like Id and Name) to Insert instead of Verify, or vice versa for request values.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Request values (sku, usernameOrEmail, userPassword) use Insert. Response values you're checking (Id, Name) use Verify.

examPitfalls.title: Confusing {CP[...]} with {XL[...]}
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Candidates assume every value must come from a linked TestSheet ({XL[...]}), missing that {CP[Email]}/{CP[Password]} are reusable Configuration Parameters usable without any TestSheet link.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: {CP[...]} pulls from project-wide Configuration Parameters (e.g. shared login credentials); {XL[...]} pulls from a linked TestSheet Instance. They're independent mechanisms.

examPitfalls.title: Leaving leftover Values next to a newly-linked XL path
examPitfalls.trapDescription: After linking TestSheet Attributes to TestStepValues in Exercise 8b, candidates don't notice an old static Value still sitting alongside the new XL reference.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: After linking, check each TestStepValue and delete any extra/leftover Value that isn't the new XL reference.

practiceQuiz.scenario: How were the raw API TestCases in this lesson originally generated?

options.text: By manually typing every TestStep from scratch.
By scanning the application's API with Tosca's API Scan feature, collecting Request/Response pairs, and exporting the result.
By importing a Swagger file directly with no further steps needed.
By recording a UI session and converting it automatically.

practiceQuiz.hint: The developers had already done this preparation step.
practiceQuiz.rationale: API TestCases are generated via Tosca's API Scan feature, which collects relevant Request/Response pairs from the application and exports them as a raw TestCase needing cleanup.

practiceQuiz.scenario: What is the one key structural difference between an API TestCase and a UI TestCase in Tosca?

options.text: API TestCases can only be run manually, never via ExecutionLists.
API TestCases cannot be converted into Templates.
API TestCases don't use TestSheets or Conditions.
Each API Message must be expressed as a Request and Response TestStep pair.

practiceQuiz.hint: Think of the restaurant analogy — an order and its response.
practiceQuiz.rationale: In API TestCases, every function-performing Message needs a matching Request and Response TestStep pair — this is the key difference from UI TestCases. Everything else in the workflow is the same.

practiceQuiz.scenario: Once an API TestCase's TestSteps are cleaned up and renamed, how does the rest of the Template-building process compare to UI TestCases?

options.text: API Templates require a completely separate Instantiate command.
API Templates skip the Check Template step entirely.
It's identical: link the TestSheet, link Values, add Conditions, Check Template, then Instantiate.
API Templates cannot use Conditions.

practiceQuiz.hint: The mechanics are the same; only the TestStep type (Request/Response) differs.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Aside from the Request/Response pairing requirement, the Template workflow — linking the TestSheet and Values, adding Conditions, Check Template, and Instantiate — is exactly the same as for UI TestCases.

practiceQuiz.scenario: Which course should you take if you want to go deeper into Tosca's API Scan capabilities specifically?

options.text: "Automation Specialist Level 1 (AS1)"
"Test Design Specialist Level 1"
"Automation Specialist for API"
There is no follow-up course for API testing.

practiceQuiz.hint: It's a course specifically dedicated to API testing depth.
practiceQuiz.rationale: The 'Automation Specialist for API' course covers API Scan and API testing capabilities in more depth than AS2.

practiceQuiz.scenario: In the "Verify Product by SKU" TestCase, what does {CP[Email]} represent?

options.text: A reusable, project-wide Configuration Parameter — like a shared login credential — independent of any TestSheet.
A link to an Instance on a linked TestSheet.
A buffered value from an earlier TestStep.
An invalid syntax that Tosca will reject.

practiceQuiz.hint: Notice this value is used in Exercise 8a, before any TestSheet is linked.
practiceQuiz.rationale: {CP[...]} pulls from a Configuration Parameter — a reusable, project-wide value like login credentials — usable in any TestStepValue without linking a TestSheet. This is different from {XL[...]} (TestSheet link) and {B[...]} (buffered value).

practiceQuiz.scenario: In "GetProductBySku Response", what ActionMode should the Id and Name TestStepValues use?

options.text: Insert
Verify
Buffer
WaitOn

practiceQuiz.hint: You're checking what came back, not sending data.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Response values are checked against expected results, so they use ActionMode Verify. Insert is for request/input values like sku, usernameOrEmail, and userPassword.

practiceQuiz.scenario: What must you do before dragging and dropping TestSheet Values onto the API Template in Exercise 8b?

options.text: Delete the existing Values in the TestStepValues first.
Set the WorkState to COMPLETED first.
Resolve every Reference in the TestCase.
Nothing — Tosca automatically replaces old values with new XL references.

practiceQuiz.hint: This is the same rule that applies everywhere else in this course.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Tosca appends a new XL reference to the end of an existing value rather than replacing it — so the existing Value must be deleted first.

practiceQuiz.scenario: After linking the TestSheet Attributes to the TestStepValues in Exercise 8b, what should you check for?

options.text: Any extra/leftover Value still sitting next to the newly-linked XL path, and delete it.
Whether the Module was renamed to "GetProductBySku Response".
Whether the ExecutionList folder exists.
Nothing further is needed once the XL reference is visible.

practiceQuiz.hint: Linking can leave a stray value behind if the field wasn't fully cleared.
practiceQuiz.rationale: If a leftover static Value remains alongside the new XL reference after linking, it must be deleted — otherwise the TestStepValue may not behave as intended.

options.text: They include both network dependent and independent APIs
APIs that require a network to operate
APIs that do not require a network to operate
Tosca functionalities that allow us to test websites

practiceQuiz.hint: It's the narrower of the two API categories — the one that needs a connection.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Web services are the subset of APIs that specifically require a network to operate (e.g. HTTP-based Request/Response calls) — unlike local/native APIs, which can run without any network.

options.text: Application Processing Intelligence
Application Programming Input
Application Programming Interface
Application Processing Information

practiceQuiz.hint: The last word describes what connects two applications — a boundary they talk across.
practiceQuiz.rationale: API stands for Application Programming Interface — a set of rules that lets applications communicate with each other, with or without a network (web services being the network-dependent subset).

practiceQuiz.scenario: Why do we need to do API Testing?

options.text: A function is available but doesn't have an UI
So we can read the code
API testing does not require Internet connection
We don't need to do API testing as everything can be accessed through the UI

practiceQuiz.hint: Think back to the SKU field — you couldn't see it anywhere on the DemoWebShop UI.
practiceQuiz.rationale: API Testing lets you verify functionality that exists in the system but has no UI to test it through — like checking a product's SKU, which isn't shown anywhere on the DemoWebShop screens.
